rationale: C19 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child: both are brief presidential letters confirming that the recipient will represent the President at a named commemorative event, followed by a short explanation of the occasion and a warm closing. The closely parallel wording about representing the President at ceremonies or a parade is more specific than routine correspondence boilerplate. C13 is also notably similar in its commemoration of a foreign-born military hero associated with American liberty, while C14 shares the personal-representative appointment machinery but concerns a continuing diplomatic mission rather than ceremonial representation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I understand that you have agreed to act as my personal representative at the Pulaski Day Parade to be held in New York on October seventh.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am delighted to know that you can represent me at the ceremonies to be held in Europe during July
shared_material.explanation: Both open by confirming the addressee's agreement to represent the President at specifically identified forthcoming ceremonies.

shared_material.child_excerpt: it is an honor for all Americans to join in observation of the anniversary of the death of the distinguished Pole who laid down his life in the cause of our liberty
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the cemeteries and the memorials it has constructed to the Americans who gave their lives in their country's service in World War II
shared_material.explanation: Each explains the representative assignment through a memorial occasion honoring those who died in service to American freedom or the country.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Thank you for acting for me on this important occasion. With warm regard
shared_material.parent_excerpt: General North, the Secretary of the Commission, can advise you in more detail concerning specific plans and arrangements. With warm regard
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude the short ceremonial-assignment letter immediately after discussing the occasion, using the same closing formula.
